record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Find new proofs that random walk in random environment scales to Brownian motion in dimensions greater than 2.

evidence.quote: Find new proofs that random walk in random environment scales to Brownian motion in d > 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ and let $(\omega(x,\cdot))_{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d}$ be an i.i.d. family of probability vectors on the $2d$ unit nearest-neighbor vectors of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, defined on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$; this family is called a random environment. Given a realization $\omega \in \Omega$, the random walk in the random environment $\omega$ started at $0$ is the Markov chain $(X_n)_{n \geq 0}$ on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $X_0 = 0$ and quenched transition probabilities $P^\omega(X_{n+1} = x + e \mid X_n = x) = \omega(x, e)$ for each nearest-neighbor unit vector $e$. Assume the environment is uniformly elliptic (there exists $\kappa > 0$ such that $\omega(x,e) \geq \kappa$ almost surely for all $x$ and all nearest-neighbor unit vectors $e$) and balanced or, more generally, satisfies a suitable non-degeneracy/centering assumption ensuring no ballistic drift on average.

Define the diffusively rescaled process $B^{(n)}(t) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigl(X_{\lfloor nt \rfloor} - \mathbb{E}^\omega[X_{\lfloor nt \rfloor}]\bigr)$, $t \geq 0$.

Provide a new proof, distinct from existing arguments based on the Kipnis–Varadhan method, environment-viewed-from-the-particle stationarity, or renormalization-group/multiscale perturbative analysis, that for $\mathbb{P}$-almost every environment $\omega$ the process $B^{(n)}$ converges in distribution, as $n \to \infty$, on the Skorokhod space $D([0,\infty); \mathbb{R}^d)$ to a non-degenerate Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with some deterministic covariance matrix $\Sigma$.
artifact.status_search_result: The invariance principle for random walks in random environments in dimensions $d > 2$ is known only under restrictive assumptions (e.g., small perturbations of simple random walk via renormalization, balanced environments, or reversible/divergence-free settings). A general proof remains an active research area, and finding genuinely new proof techniques is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Random Walks, Scaling Limits and Criticality (Herrsching 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Workshop abstracts indicate diffusive scaling limits and invariance principles for random walks in random environments remain an active research topic.
status_evidence.claim: Scaling limits of RWRE in d>2 are still being actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Brownian motion limit of random walks in symmetric non-homogeneous media
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions for a scaled random walk on a non-homogeneous medium to converge to Brownian motion are discussed, with only partial results in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are available for the invariance principle in higher dimensions.
